chapter: Changing styles, the road and nightlife
title: Chicago hangouts and breakfast dances
summary: Musicians hung out in clubs and rotated through breakfast dances at DeLisa, Plotnik's, Cabin Inn and Rum Boogie, swapping jobs.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: There used to be some places where guys hung out, wasn't there?

Well, I mean, we had so many places here. I mean, like -- well, they hung out in the clubs. It didn't cost them hardly anything, and everybody knew everybody, everybody was friendly and if you were busted it still didn't make any difference because you could go in and get a

drink, and next time it was your turn to pop. So everybody felt free to come out and go, and all of the clubs, a bunch hanging out -- that's what they used when they had the breakfast shows. At one time, I remember, in the -- well, I guess in the late '40s and the early '50s and things, they had breakfast dances, one every morning. Every morning, the Club DeLisa on a Sunday, going into Monday morning, then Monday night they had a place called Plotnik's and he would be like on a Monday, and Tuesday they'd go to the Cabin Inn. That's where all them gay show was. And it was like that. And then we went to the Rum Boogie on Saturday ~~ and ~~ Sunday morning.

So every day, it was that thing. And then, this was -- not only did you go there, you exchanged jobs. It was like a booking office, almost. Because you could pick up a job or you got the information that so-and-so is closing, and it was good for that.
